name: Ch’üan Te-yü
bio: Ch’üan Te-yü (AD 759–818) was a T’ang official and poet. His poem here is a brief verse addressed to a bride.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Hope
poems.author: Ch’üan Te-yü
poems.text:
Last eve thou wert a bride,
This morn thy dream is o'er
Cast not thy rouge aside,
He may be thine once more.

poems.title: The Jade Dressing-Table
poems.author: Ch’üan Te-yü
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Last night my girdle came undone,
And this morning a luck-beetle flew over my bed.
So here are my paints and here are my powders —
And a welcome for my yoke again.

poems.title: 玉臺體 (Yu tai ti)
poems.author: Ch’üan Te-yü
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
昨夜裙帶解，今朝蟢子飛。
鉛華不可棄，莫是藁砧歸。
